_meta.status: SEED — VERIFIED ENTRIES ONLY, NOT EXHAUSTIVE
_meta.description: Auction houses and agencies documented as channels for Nazi-era confiscated/forced-sale art. A match here is a signal to check the specific transaction, not an accusation against the entity generally — several of these are real businesses still operating today, and most Nazi-era-documented auction houses handled both legitimate and forced/looted transactions. See critical_context for required framing.
_meta.critical_context: Mention of one of these entities in a provenance record is not itself evidence of a forced sale or looting — several sources explicitly warn against treating mere name-mention as proof (see Lempertz entry). Every match must be rendered with the specific historical basis cited below, and the object's own transaction_state/date/circumstances must be evaluated on their own evidence, not inferred solely from the venue.
_meta.gate_field_note: `implies_persecution_of_former_owner` was added per documented_basis limb so the matching logic can carry the distinction this file states in prose, rather than leaving it to a reader. Each value is transcribed from that entry's own basis text and carries a `gate_basis` quoting why; no new claim is made about any entity. The Galerie Fischer basis was split into its two limbs exactly where the entry itself says 'Separately,' — both texts are preserved verbatim. Like everything else here, this needs confirmation from a provenance researcher before production use.

entries.name: Weinmüller (Münchener Kunstversteigerungshaus Adolf Weinmüller)

documented_basis.summary: Aryanized two Jewish-owned auction houses — Hugo Helbing's in Munich (1936) and the Kende family's in Vienna (1938) — and subsequently auctioned art seized from Jewish dealers and collectors, including consigned Gestapo-seized property (e.g. the Laemmle collection). Investigated post-war by the ALIU and listed as a Red Flag Name. Predecessor to the present-day Neumeister auction house, Munich.
documented_basis.gate_basis: TRUE per the entry's own words: the entry's own basis states the house 'auctioned art seized from Jewish dealers and collectors, including consigned Gestapo-seized property'.

entries.verification_note: Strongly corroborated across Bavarian state provenance research project, JDCRP, CNN, and Wikipedia independently.

entries.name: Galerie Fischer (Lucerne)
entries.active_period: Specifically flagged: 30 June 1939 auction. Broader wartime activity separately documented.

documented_basis.summary: IMPORTANT DISTINCTION — do not conflate: the 30 June 1939 sale at the Grand Hotel National specifically auctioned 'Degenerate Art' confiscated by the Nazi state from GERMAN STATE MUSEUMS (not privately-owned Jewish collections) — a different legal category from persecuted-individual forced sales.
documented_basis.period: 30 June 1939 auction, Grand Hotel National, Lucerne
documented_basis.gate_basis: FALSE per the entry's own words: the works auctioned were confiscated from GERMAN STATE MUSEUMS, not privately-owned collections, which the entry itself calls 'a different legal category from persecuted-individual forced sales'.

documented_basis.summary: Separately, Wikipedia's biography of Theodor Fischer states he 'played a key part in the trading of art looted by the Germans from occupied countries' during the broader war period — this is a distinct claim about private/looted (not state 'degenerate art') property and needs its own case-level verification, not assumed from the 1939 sale alone.
documented_basis.gate_basis: FALSE per the entry's own words: this limb 'needs its own case-level verification, not assumed from the 1939 sale alone'. It is single-sourced and cannot carry an inference about any specific object's former owner.

entries.verification_note: The 30 June 1939 date/venue/category is very strongly corroborated (5+ independent sources). The broader wartime looted-art-trading claim is single-sourced (Wikipedia) — verify independently before relying on it for anything beyond the 1939 state-museum sale specifically.

entries.name: Lempertz (Cologne)

documented_basis.summary: Listed by the ALIU as a Red Flag Name in 1946. Documented case: Nazis forced dealer Max Stern to consign several hundred works from his family's Düsseldorf gallery to Lempertz for a Nazi-sanctioned forced sale (Dec 1939), including a 1632 Dutch portrait later subject to restitution research (Wikidata-documented). Still an operating auction house — this entry is about specific historical transactions, not a characterization of the current business.
documented_basis.gate_basis: TRUE per the entry's own words: the entry's own basis states 'Nazis forced dealer Max Stern to consign several hundred works ... for a Nazi-sanctioned forced sale'.

entries.verification_note: ALIU listing and Max Stern case both independently corroborated. Note explicitly that mere name-mention in a provenance record is not itself evidence — cited source explicitly warns of this.

entries.name: Dorotheum (Vienna)

documented_basis.summary: Documented as a co-venue (with Weinmüller in Munich) for auctioning cultural assets seized from Jews and other Nazi-designated 'enemies of the state' at Gestapo headquarters, Prague, per a June 1941 inspection commission.
documented_basis.gate_basis: TRUE per the entry's own words: the entry's own basis states the venue auctioned 'cultural assets seized from Jews and other Nazi-designated ‘enemies of the state’'.

entries.verification_note: WEAKER SOURCING than the other entries — corroborated only via the Weinmüller research (two sources, both discussing Dorotheum as a secondary detail, not a dedicated Dorotheum-focused source). Get a dedicated citation before treating as fully verified.

entries.name: Sonderauftrag Linz
entries.location: Linz, Austria (planned museum); acquisitions made across Europe

documented_basis.summary: Hitler's personal art-acquisition project for a planned museum in Linz; well-established organizational entity in Nazi art appropriation, corroborated across numerous independent historical sources.
documented_basis.gate_basis: TRUE per the entry's own words: the entry's own basis describes a 'well-established organizational entity in Nazi art appropriation'.

entries.verification_note: Extremely well-established historical entity, corroborated across 5+ independent sources encountered during research. No further verification needed.

entries.name: ERR (Einsatzstab Reichsleiter Rosenberg)
entries.location: Primarily France; operated across occupied territories

documented_basis.summary: The primary Nazi organizational agency for art confiscation in occupied territories, overseen by the ALIU's own investigative reports (CIR No. 1, Aug 1945). Well-established, uncontroversial historical entity.
documented_basis.gate_basis: TRUE per the entry's own words: the entry's own basis describes 'the primary Nazi organizational agency for art confiscation in occupied territories'.

entries.verification_note: Extremely well-established historical entity, corroborated across numerous independent sources encountered during research. No further verification needed.
